column6: Series-wide evidence note: zero Apple sample code — guides rest on shipped repo source, docs prose, and SDK dumps
optimize() deletes a broadcasting-significant expand_dims — 17 dB PSNR at model scale, shape still validates (issue #49)
Unmatched ExternalizeSpec warns, never raises — a typo ships a slower model; assert on composite_declaration in the IR
MTLTensor extents reverse the torch shape — a kernel correct in torch coordinates reads the wrong axes in Metal
Evidence note: no Apple sample code — strongest sources are the shipped coreai-torch/models/optimization repos
OS 27 beta 2 refuses .aimodel files converted with coreai-torch v0.4.0 — published assets must be reconverted with 0.4.1
torch.cond / while_loop convert but run only on the bundled interpreter — no cpu/gpu/ane runtime support today
The 'three preserved ops' claim is wrong as commonly stated — see the corrected preserved-op list
torch.export's default decomposition table splits SDPA into matmul+softmax — you silently lose the fused kernel
No error marks a lost composite — count ops with freqop or assert composite.scaled_dot_product_attention in the IR
Naming parameters are keyword-only; the API doc renders them positionally — positional calls raise TypeError
export_fn is keyword-only and required — the API doc shows it positionally and with no hint that it has no default
ExternalizeSpec target_class must be RMSNormImpl — pointing at the RMSNorm wrapper silently matches nothing
optimize() is not always semantics-preserving — a deleted expand_dims changes results while shapes still validate
Distance matrices, Gram matrices and contrastive forms are exposed — gate optimize=True vs False on real inputs
Apple material shows both runner(**inputs) and runner(dict) calling conventions — pick the dict form the tests use
input_names/output_names no longer cover buffers — pre-release conversion scripts now fail the count check
Omitted I/O names get FX placeholder defaults — an implementation detail, not a contract, that changes across PyTorch
A PyTorch upgrade renames auto-generated keys or rebinds them to different tensors — pass explicit names everywhere
State ordering is an assumption — same-shape buffers like k_cache/v_cache can swap slots and every check still passes
k_cache and v_cache can swap positions across a PyTorch upgrade — Swift binds key to the value slot and output is garbage
NDArray.from_descriptor only sizes the buffer — on Linux, buffer-state reads return garbage on the first call
The Neural Engine path threads K/V as plain I/O, not Core AI state — register_buffer KV advice is GPU-only
Session 325 says 4-bit on both encoders; the shipped recipe is asymmetric (image w4/gs32, text w6/gs8)
Entrypoint names are routing: nonstandard names make the loader classify .dynamic and request GPU instead of ANE
The 76% faster second inference requires caller-side caching Apple's own package does not implement
CoreAISegmentationEngine re-runs image_encode every segment() and exposes no way to hold backbone features
AIModelAsset.load only reads the header — compilation and its cost land lazily inside the executable() context manager
The standing gate: convert twice (optimize on/off), run both at real shapes, fail the build on output divergence
Gate with realistic inputs — issue #49 does not reproduce on 17x23 rectangles, only on square production shapes
inspect succeeding is not evidence the asset will compile or load on-device (see the version gate)
TorchConverter's mode= parameter is real but absent from the API doc — as is the strip_debug_info escape hatch
Docstring examples still call dump_intermediates — the exported symbol is save_intermediates; suffix is validated
Preview-only env vars gate debug metadata — set them before conversion or tooling loses attribution
Without ENABLE_DEBUG_INFO=1, metadata is silently absent — the Debugger's navigator and source viewer just come up empty
The pipeline listing is a toy exercising every contract — run the optimize gate separately at your real shapes
v0.4.0-converted artifacts fail to load from OS 27 beta 2 — reconvert with coreai-torch v0.4.1 or later
Seventeen open defects across the repos produce plausible, correct-shaped output with no diagnostic — four still unfixed
Coverage is per-overload — support for one overload of an op proves nothing about its siblings
mean.dim converts, mean.names_dim doesn't; sum.dim_IntList converts, sum.default is absent from the table entirely
clone()/contiguous() lower to identity — barrier-by-clone silently does nothing against the buffer-clobber bug (#11)
torch.cond/while_loop convert but the cpu/gpu/ane runtimes cannot run them — interpreter only, a device blocker
torch.export.default_decompositions() makes conversion fail — only Apple's get_decomp_table() works
The default torch decomposition table yields unsupported ops — conversion fails; use get_decomp_table() instead
Validation is ATen-only: custom torch.library ops pass silently, then to_coreai() fails with a different error
instance_norm becomes a composite only when use_input_stats is truthy — otherwise you quietly lose the optimized kernel
A typo in composite_attrs or target_class is a UserWarning, not an error — filtered warnings ship a slower model silently
SDPA has two conversion routes with one name — their attribute schemas and mask conventions differ
The causal-mask convention differs between the two SDPA routes when query and key lengths differ — masks land wrong
Externalize RMSNormImpl, not RMSNorm — the wrapper class silently matches no submodule
RoPE requires fp32, and partial-rotary mode pairs the wrong dimensions — a known acknowledged issue
Partial-rotary RoPE pairs dims contiguously, not as checkpoints expect — wrong rotations, acknowledged as a known issue
gather_mm indices must be unsigned ints while torch.topk returns int64 — PyTorch won't complain about the mismatch
Scope note: how far MoE gather_mm support does not extend — read before assuming coverage
MoE on GPU/ANE delegates is combination-dependent — Qwen3-MoE ships, but support is not universal
Lowering overrides are per-converter-instance and invisible in output — a shared converter object carries hidden semantics
Registration ordering matters, and the rule is subtler than 'always register first'
generate-composite-decl docs name the wrong parameter (op_name), omit version, and misstate the return type
Externalization needs the live nn.Module via add_pytorch_module — add_exported_program has no externalization path
Externalized bodies are decomposed with a table you didn't choose — clean validation, then a confusing unsupported-op error
Composite input_names are parameters and buffers first, then forward args — not your forward signature order
Apple ships GatedDeltaUpdate with composite_attrs=[] — the doc page's attribute list does not match the shipped spec
Externalization is not weight streaming — it neither reduces export RAM nor mmaps; that is a separate PyTorch technique
One word, two mechanisms: ExternalizeSpec preserves op boundaries; multi-entrypoint conversion splits programs
Externalization's four silent failures — unmatched specs and attr typos warn or say nothing and quietly drop the composite
fp16 casting ignores activation overflow in softplus/mish/logsumexp — the sanctioned fix is rewriting your module
Compression shifts activation distributions — values once below the fp16 overflow threshold can newly exceed it
Integer true divide ran as int division then cast — fractions dropped on every backend (PR #32; latent twin in div)
cat on packed sub-byte tensors always concatenates on dim 0 — (2,4)+(2,4) at dim=1 silently yields (4,4), not (2,8)
sum/prod on int64 reduced in int32 — silently wrapping identically on every backend, corrupting the lowered IR
Design gate inputs to break symmetry: asymmetric shapes, values straddling zero and above 10, large integers
TorchConverter.md renders keyword-only params positionally and omits mode= — code written from the doc raises TypeError
Read first: zero Apple sample code for Core AI — kernel guidance rests on shipped coreai-torch source and tests
Set USE_LOCAL_COREAI and ENABLE_DEBUG_INFO before conversion or profiles simply lack module/source attribution
The axis reversal: MTLTensor extents are the reverse of the torch shape, and subscripts reverse too
Torch (D0,D1,D2) arrives in the kernel as (D2,D1,D0) — your correct torch_defn cannot catch the reversed Metal body
torch_defn is shape inference only — a kernel emitting zeros or NaN converts cleanly; write the numeric test yourself
A literal result_shapes under a dynamic input compiles fine — at other runtime sizes the kernel writes the stale shape
result_shapes=[2,2,3] freezes into a ?x2x3 graph — when dim 0 arrives as 7, nothing objects; use list(x.shape) always
The function containing a custom kernel is GPU-resident — splitting entrypoints pins that function off the ANE
Template substitution is textual — every occurrence of TYPE is replaced, including comments, strings, and MY_TYPE
Templating covers the type, not literals — TYPE sum = 0.0f breaks integer instantiations; template ZERO per dtype too
The shipped SAM3 export does not contain session 330's FlashAttention kernel — there is no code to copy
Quantized-kernel APIs are narrower than session 330 suggests — the feature ladder is per-point-release
Without __HAVE_TENSOR__ the whole MPP header expands to nothing — just a 'no member named matmul2d' error far downstream
torch.cond branch subgraphs never receive your registered custom lowerings — a pinned strict-xfail converter bug
A bad kernel body is not a conversion error — it fails only at function bind, without any compiler diagnostic
Malformed MSL converts, saves and loads cleanly — the bind-time failure message contains no compiler diagnostic
Apple's own end-to-end custom-kernel tests are currently disabled — device coverage is thinner than the suite implies
torch_defn is traced with FakeTensors — any value read like int(idx[i]) or .item() breaks; keep gathers shape-static
A custom kernel is a fusion barrier — the surrounding graph slows in ways your kernel's own timing never shows
Kernel edges materialize in the dtype the kernel asks for — boundary casts become real ops that inflate the graph
Naked exp() in a hand-written softmax overflows — subtract the running max first, as Apple's own fixture does
Community figures here are single-author, self-declared uncontrolled, on beta OSes — attribute, never launder
